headline: No school changed tier this run; the DHS SEVIS Help Hub, DHS CPT-guidance, Tufts and retroactive-cancellation tripwires are all unchanged on direct fetch. Davidson, MIT, Skidmore and the University of South Florida remain the only schools confirmed to have interrupted already-granted CPT; the 5 Oct CPT lawsuit against DHS remains pending, no ruling yet.

tripwires.name: DHS SEVIS Help Hub CPT page
tripwires.detail: Direct fetch succeeded again 10 Oct 06:15 UTC (10 Oct 14:15 HKT). Page unchanged, still "Last Updated: August 24, 2026," same two broadcast-message citations; cancellation section still only states a DSO can cancel CPT before its start date and, after the start date, can only edit the authorisation to shorten the end date — not cancel it outright. No mention of the 5 Oct lawsuit. No change to the page itself.

tripwires.name: Tufts I-Center CPT page
tripwires.detail: Direct fetch succeeded again 10 Oct 06:15 UTC — the "the I-Center is unable to process CPT requests for non-required internships at this time" sentence is still present, unchanged; still nothing either way about students who already hold CPT authorisation. No change detected.

tripwires.name: Federal Register rulemaking on CPT
tripwires.detail: Checked 10 Oct 06:15 UTC, direct fetch of DHS's own CPT-guidance tripwire page confirmed — still only says SEVP 'plans to release draft guidance' clarifying prior CPT documents, no date given, no mention of the lawsuit or the August broadcast messages; blog list unchanged (7 Oct OPT-fee proposed rule, 24 Sept community-colleges post, 25 Aug SEVP webinar post) — none of it a CPT rulemaking development. No CPT-specific Federal Register notice found. CPT remains guidance (12/24 Aug broadcast messages), not a rule. No new result on the 5 Oct lawsuit's injunction motion; case remains pending.

tripwires.name: Retroactive cancellation spreading
tripwires.detail: Still tripped, re-checked 10 Oct 06:15 UTC — no school newly moved into 'cancels' this run. Davidson, MIT, Skidmore and University of South Florida remain the only confirmed interruptions of already-granted CPT.

tiers.label: Already-approved CPT stopped or withdrawn
tiers.sub: The most severe response: students who already held an authorisation were told to stop work, or had it withdrawn.

context: First CPT-specific litigation: on 5 Oct a coalition (AAU, Presidents' Alliance on Higher Education and Immigration, NAFSA, AICUM) sued DHS in federal court in Massachusetts over the Aug 12/24 BCMs, calling them procedurally invalid and impermissibly retroactive, with an emergency injunction motion filed the same night seeking to block enforcement while the case proceeds; case pending, no ruling yet (NAFSA held a member town hall on the case 7 Oct). No third broadcast message. DHS's stated position: 'nothing about these regulations has changed.' ICE is auditing schools, with SEVP decertification as the stated risk. Immigration attorneys flag a retroactive-scrutiny risk — past CPT revisited at the OPT, STEM-OPT or H-1B stage. The common institutional reading of the new standard: integral to the curriculum, required of all students in the programme for degree completion, a documented cooperative agreement with the employer, and DSO authorisation before training begins.
